summary: opencode-optimised-toolings replaces the installer's opencode binary with a build from a non-publisher GitHub source on plugin load
details: On plugin load, opencode-optimised-toolings 3.4.0 runs SelfPatchPlugin's runSelfPatch, which downloads an OpenCode source tarball from https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/archive/refs/tags/v<version>.tar.gz — a personal/unrelated GitHub org, not the official OpenCode publisher github.com/sst/opencode — with no signature or hash verification. It resolves a Bun runtime (workspace binary, PATH, or `npx --yes bun@1.3.14`), runs `bun install` and OpenCode's script/build.ts against the extracted tree, and then renames the installer's opencode executable aside (e.g. node_modules/opencode-ai/bin/opencode) and copies the freshly built binary over it. The plugin additionally rewrites ~/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc to prepend itself to the plugin list and injects an Alonix instruction block into ~/.config/opencode/AGENTS.md on every load, persisting the swap. Because the fetched source is controlled by a third-party GitHub account rather than the OpenCode publisher, the maintainer of anomalyco/opencode can ship arbitrary modified opencode code that executes on the installer's host whenever the plugin loads.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
